unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Observed facts confirm complete row acceptance, unique source identifiers, and exact dollar reconciliation across both dealer import files tied to the cluster" — the cited import-log checks strongly support acceptance, reconciliation, and zero duplicate-source-event flags, but the submission does not show the underlying row-level join or query proving uniqueness for every recharge row.

"This resolves the duplicate-revenue and pipeline-defect hypotheses with high confidence" — zero duplicate-source-event flags and zero reconciliation differences substantially reduce duplicate-import risk, but they do not rule out every possible pipeline defect or manipulation mechanism.

"the transactions themselves occurred on their actual dates throughout May" — effective_event_date and the dealer email support the posting-time explanation, but they do not independently prove the actual occurrence date.

"Revenue manipulation / period-stuffing: rejected" because all effective dates fall within May — this rules out obvious cross-period pulling or pushing, but does not fully exclude manipulation occurring within the same month.

"this same zero-variance pattern holds across all 41 logged files for these two dealers going back to January" — the evidence table says the monthly pattern is observed "Since March 2026," creating an apparent January/March inconsistency.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the strongest benign alternative well: two dealers batch annual-plan files at month-end while retaining original effective dates. The main missed alternative is that within-month manipulation or a defect outside duplicate-source-event handling could remain possible even when effective dates stay within May and import reconciliation is zero.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Narrow the causal conclusions and provide a reproducible row-level join/query showing each clustered recharge maps to exactly one accepted source_event_id and ledger amount, while explicitly treating within-month manipulation and non-import pipeline defects as unresolved rather than rejected.

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "What operationally happens to a customer whose IVR session ends in ERROR or ABANDONED at or before authentication — is there a logged follow-up channel?"
"What is the written pass/fail threshold and minimum observation window for moving NovaIVR to national rollout?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "the issues didn't disappear, only their ticket visibility did" is too definitive: service-event counts remaining within a historical range do not establish that the same customer issues persisted or that no issues were resolved through another channel.

"the ~932 failed-session subscribers who never recontact via IVR or ticket within 7 days" is not reproducible from the stated figures: 1,098 minus 166 minus 13 equals 919 before accounting for overlap, and the submission does not explain the distinct-subscriber and overlap calculation.
The claim that 464 of 650 pre-authentication sessions ended in ERROR/ABANDONED is cited only indirectly and should have a more explicit outcome-by-authentication cross-tab or query definition.

The conclusion that the drop is "largely" an artifact is well supported as a measurement concern, but the available evidence does not quantify how much of the ticket reduction reflects missing capture versus genuine resolution.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission handled the strongest benign alternative: failed or abandoned sessions may have been resolved through dealer contact, agent callback, or another untracked channel. It preserved this as an unknown and proposed checking those channels. It could have more explicitly treated genuine self-service resolution of successfully completed sessions as a separate alternative rather than focusing mainly on failed-session outcomes; abandonment itself is not proof of a complaint or unresolved friction.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Reconcile and document the subscriber-level outcome accounting for the 1,098 ERROR/ABANDONED sessions—including deduplication and overlap between repeat IVR and ticket contacts—and link those sessions to dealer, callback, resolution, or churn outcomes before describing the ticket decline as an artifact.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: Submission quotes: "all 4 rows have impact_mw=0 and cleared=yes" and cites inverter_events.csv, rows 1–4, impact_mw, cleared.
Submission also cites inverter_events.csv rows 1–4 for severity, event, duration_min, timestamps, and inverter_id; key observations are separated from the low-confidence completeness inference.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: Submission cross-checks severity, duration, cleared status, impact_mw, inverter identity, and dates rather than relying only on the warning label.

It tests the innocent data-scope explanation by noting that "Extraction filters are unknown" and proposing an unfiltered read-only export, but it does not corroborate the event data with an independent operational channel.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: Submission assigns high confidence to the observed zero-impact/cleared fields and low confidence to representativeness: "The export spans 27 May–4 June ... but contains only 4 rows and no plant-wide denominator or extraction filter."
It explicitly limits the conclusion to current evidence and states what would change the decision: additional open faults, recurrence, critical severity, or nonzero impact.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation—"Hold escalation and execute one cheap completeness check"—is proportionate to four short, cleared, zero-impact events.
The proposed read-only export query without status filters is reversible and discriminates between an incomplete extract and a genuinely quiet event set.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion that escalation is unsupported on current evidence matches the cited facts: four events, distinct inverters, durations of 1–7 minutes, cleared=yes, and impact_mw=0.
The submission does not invent a plant problem from the seven-minute communications warning and preserves a conditional path to re-evaluation if the completeness check reveals stronger evidence.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Zero repeat pattern" is true only within the four-row extract; because extraction completeness is unknown, it should not be treated as evidence that recurrence did not occur.
"Zero generation loss" slightly overstates what is directly shown unless impact_mw is explicitly defined as generation loss; the directly supported claim is zero recorded impact_mw.
"Fully cleared telemetry" is broader than the row-level cleared=yes field and could be phrased as four recorded events marked cleared.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The COMM_LINK_WARN may represent an intermittent communications or telemetry-quality issue rather than physical inverter damage, while an incomplete or filtered export could still conceal recurrence or higher-severity events. The submission appropriately treats this as a completeness question rather than a reason to escalate immediately.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Tighten the evidence language and verify the export schema and completeness metadata: distinguish recorded impact_mw=0 from actual generation loss, and distinguish no repeats in this extract from no recurrence in the plant.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites AI_Pilot_Impact_Note.md's comparison table and observed-difference line for Rs 662,444 versus Rs 453,086 and the 31.6% figure.
It identifies dispatch_blocks.csv and the dsm_penalty_rs field as the source for independently reproducing both daily totals.
It specifically cites base_schedule_mw, submitted_schedule_mw, and actual_mw in dispatch_blocks.csv plus the DSM_Commercial_Extract.pdf deviation-band table for the 17.6% same-day modeled estimate.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission distinguishes the different-day comparison from a same-day base_schedule_mw versus submitted_schedule_mw counterfactual on 29 May.
It cross-checks the headline arithmetic against the underlying CSV rather than accepting the impact note's summary.
It tests plausible alternative explanations, especially whether revisions were made before generation was known and whether the apparent DSM benefit survives full net-settlement accounting.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: It explicitly labels 31.6% as a two-day arithmetic comparison and 17.6% as a single-day modeled estimate rather than a causal estimate.
It assigns different confidence levels to arithmetic and causal interpretation and identifies the unknown timing of the 12 revisions as decision-changing evidence.
It preserves a smaller positive same-day signal instead of concluding that the pilot has no value.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to maintain the current scope and defer fleet or national expansion follows from the limited one-day, model-based evidence.

The proposed next measurement is reversible and operationally safe: pre-register additional high-wind days, capture immutable pre-submission timestamps, repeat the shadow calculation, and include full net commercial value.
The submission specifies how positive and negative test results would change the decision.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion accurately states that the 31.6% result compares 28 May with 29 May and does not establish that the pilot caused the reduction.
It gives the appropriately narrower conclusion that 29 May shows an approximately 17.6% modeled reduction for the revised blocks against the retained base schedule.
It avoids overcorrecting to 'no value' while appropriately withholding expansion pending stronger evidence.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The characterization of 28 May as a 'cherry-picked high-penalty comparator' is stronger than the supplied evidence establishes: being the worst conventional day shows comparator risk, but not intentional cherry-picking.

The statement that the 17.6% claim is 'contradicted' by the lack of repeated observations is imprecise; the lack of repetition limits generalizability and causal confidence but does not contradict the one-day modeled result.

The statement that repeated pre-registered testing is 'the only way' to distinguish genuine forecast skill from a one-off favorable day is overly absolute; other evidence, such as matched historical controls or audited decision timestamps, could also help.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 31.6% difference may mainly reflect the unusually severe 28 May comparator, while the 17.6% same-day modeled difference could still represent genuine pilot value. The current evidence supports retaining that possibility, but not estimating a general causal effect or expanding the pilot.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Explicitly test comparability of 28 and 29 May and other high-wind days using wind conditions, forecast error, curtailment, and dispatch context, alongside the already proposed immutable revision timestamps. This would distinguish day-severity effects from a reproducible pilot mechanism.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "CHF 126,900 total closes it" is unsupported: the submission does not establish why the invoice total resolves the classification or value-presentation question.

"Preference=Yes on the declaration is sufficient on its own": rejected because the declaration field carries no linked supplier evidence

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "Until sourcing is confirmed, the claim is unsupported — and could range from fully documented to actively inconsistent with the register, depending on which supplier this was."
"IF POSITIVE (SUP-01 confirmed): origin claim is fully supported by a current, matching register entry, clear the claim."

"IF NEGATIVE (SUP-02/03/05/06 confirmed instead): declared origin of United States matches none of those suppliers' registered origins, escalate from documentation gap to potential origin-misdeclaration review."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Air waybill links SHP-000411 to IE-2025-000411 but carries no supplier_id field"
"Automated flag: 'Preference indicator present. Supplier support not linked in ClearView.'"
"Confirming the supplier first is the higher-value, equally cheap step"

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Place a reversible hold on the preference claim and request the shipment-specific sourcing record"
"before requesting any supplier declaration"
"The declaration already shows 0.0% duty regardless of preference status, so this hold changes no duty amount"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "IF POSITIVE (SUP-01 confirmed): origin claim is fully supported by a current, matching register entry, clear the claim." A current register row and supplier identity do not by themselves establish shipment-specific preferential origin; the submission also needs the applicable supplier declaration or equivalent origin evidence.

The submission treats the invoice's "manufacturing country" and the register's "registered origin" as sufficient proxies for preferential origin without explicitly distinguishing manufacturing country from preferential origin or explaining the applicable preference rule.

"The declaration already shows 0.0% duty regardless of preference status" is not established merely because the declaration states 0.0% duty alongside Preference=Yes; the effect of removing preference should be verified rather than assumed.

"Genuine origin discrepancy" if a non-SUP-01 supplier is confirmed is too definitive because a register mismatch establishes a discrepancy requiring review, not necessarily the actual origin or a misdeclaration.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The shipment may have been manufactured in the United States, as stated on the commercial invoice, while preferential origin still remains unproven because the supplier and shipment-specific origin support are not linked. Conversely, a non-US register row may reflect outdated or incomplete register data rather than the shipment's actual origin. The safest supported conclusion is therefore to hold the preference claim pending both supplier linkage and shipment-specific preferential-origin evidence.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Explicitly distinguish manufacturing country from preferential origin and make supplier-specific documentary evidence, not merely confirmation of SUP-01 in the register, a prerequisite to clearing the preference claim.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Calling all 185 02:10:00 timestamps "snapshot artifacts" is stronger than the available evidence strictly proves; the recurring timestamp pattern strongly supports that interpretation, but live audit or event-level records are still needed.

The claim that excluding open rows biases the 45.5-hour figure downward is plausible given their recent receipt dates, but their eventual durations are not yet observed, so the magnitude and direction should remain explicitly conditional.
The statement that 02:10:00-stamped rows are "not real disposition times" should remain a hypothesis until QCore audit or an event log confirms timestamp semantics.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10:00 values could represent genuine operational batch-disposition times rather than an interface default, in which case the long cycle times may reflect real waiting or batch-release behavior. A second live timestamp or event-log comparison is needed to distinguish that explanation from interface-timing distortion.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain a small event-level sample containing receipt, evidence-available, decision/disposition, and QCore interface-commit timestamps, with source snapshot metadata. This would simultaneously test the SOP clock, distinguish workflow delay from interface timing, and establish whether the extracts can support a launchable KPI.

"BLT-7302 rev A combined demand (702+707+718 = 5 units) exceeds confirmed clean supply (1 unit)"; "spare_parts.csv, part_restrictions.csv, part_requests.csv, joined by MPN/revision"

The submission gives specific files, fields, request IDs, part numbers, revisions, quantities, restrictions, freshness dates, and acknowledges uncertainty around sentinel values.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "Every MPN match is a direct transfer opportunity: rejected because BLT-7302 rev A demand (5 units, 3 requests) exceeds confirmed clean supply (1 unit)"
"MTR-4401 rev A has zero usable path: HA-0002 avail=0; ME-0003 avail=1 but reserved_for_critical_asset=true"
"PR-260703 ... demand 2 exactly matches clean supply 2 ... but PR-260713/723 may compete for the same part"

The analyst separates identity matching from pooled availability, revision, reservations, and sentinel handling, and tests competing-demand explanations. However, it does not investigate whether semantic matching could provide useful candidate identities for the blank-MPN requests.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "Stock snapshot ... dated 2026-06-26 ... vs request export ... 2026-07-24"
"Actionable now" for several matches despite the stated stale global stock snapshot
"-1 ... treated as a verification sentinel ... Confidence: Medium"

The analyst notices source-age and data-quality limitations and identifies evidence that could change decisions, but the 'actionable now' classification is too strong without a current availability/reservation check. Confidence is not consistently downgraded for the temporal inconsistency.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Do not convert search hits into automatic transfers"
"13 of 24 requests already carry an exact, joinable manufacturer part number"
"The real constraint is that the other 11 requests have a blank manufacturer_part_no field"
"confirmed as an existing MPN with clean stock -> actionable; confirmed as no match or an exhausted pool ... -> not transferable"

The recommendation usefully reframes automatic transfer into controlled candidate/actionability decisions and protects against pooled-demand and restriction risks. It is weakened by the categorical recommendation not to fund even a small, safeguarded semantic-search candidate-generation pilot for the blank-MPN population.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "Every MPN match is a direct transfer opportunity"; rejected using the BLT-7302 shared-pool calculation
"An expensive semantic-search system is needed"; rejected because 13 of 24 requests already carry an exact, joinable part number
"Description similarity confirms MTR-4401 identity for blank-MPN requests"; rejected because identity must be confirmed per policy

The submission actively tests several plausible interpretations and explains why they fail, but it does not test the strongest competing explanation that semantic search could generate useful identity candidates without authorizing transfers.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "EVIDENCE NEEDED: manufacturer part number and revision from local maintenance records"
"EVIDENCE NEEDED: live CMMS/MaintStar query"
"This would change my decision as follows" followed by specific classification changes

The requested evidence is prioritized and tied to decision changes. The next-evidence plan omits a small evaluation of description-to-catalog retrieval quality for the 11 blank-MPN requests, which would directly discriminate whether a semantic pilot has value.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Do not ... fund a semantic-search pilot" is too categorical: exact MPN joins resolve 13 requests but do not establish that semantic search cannot generate useful candidate identities for the 11 blank-MPN requests.

The classification "Actionable now" is overstated given that MaintStar-global stock is dated 2026-06-26 while the request export is dated 2026-07-24; current availability, reservations, and criticality should be confirmed before action.
"No search algorithm can resolve" the 11 blank-MPN requests is unsupported. Search may not establish identity by itself, but it can produce candidates for engineering or maintenance confirmation.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Semantic search remains useful as a constrained candidate-generation tool for the 11 blank-MPN requests, even if it cannot independently authorize transfers. A small benchmark could measure top-k identity-retrieval precision, with revision, qualification, reservation, pooled-demand, and current-availability checks retained as separate gates.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run a reversible pilot on the 11 blank-MPN requests: normalize descriptions, generate top-k catalog candidates, have maintenance or engineering confirm identity and revision, then recheck live availability and restrictions. Measure confirmed-identity yield and actionable-value uplift against the exact-MPN baseline before deciding whether to fund broader deployment.
